// Ball Drone flight-assistance bridge for ESP32-S3 (Freenove): protocol version 1 over USB serial.
//
// Speaks the same ASCII HELLO/READY/CMD/ACK protocol as firmware/PROTOCOL.md using the shared C core
// (src/core.c) and line framing (src/line_reader.c), identical to the Arduino Mega version.
//
// PPM TRAINER OUTPUT on GPIO 4.  An 8-channel CPPM waveform is generated by a hardware timer
// interrupt.  Only the yaw channel (RC ch 4) carries the accepted yaw value; all other channels stay
// centered.  A safety jumper from GPIO 5 to GND must be present to arm the output; removing it holds
// the line idle (steady HIGH, no falling edges) so the radio's trainer port sees no valid signal.
//
// The ESP32-S3 outputs 3.3 V logic, matching the RadioMaster Pocket's trainer input directly.
// No voltage divider is needed — GPIO 4 wires straight to the 3.5 mm cable tip.
//
// The USB/UART port provides the serial connection to the Raspberry Pi.  On the Freenove ESP32-S3
// board, this is the port labeled "USB/UART" (left side when viewed from the top).
#include "src/core.h"
#include "src/line_reader.h"
#include "ppm.h"

static ball_core core;
static ball_line reader;
static char reply[160];

void setup() {
    Serial.begin(9600);
    ball_init(&core);
    ball_line_init(&reader);
    ppm_init();
}

void loop() {
    uint32_t now = millis();
    ball_tick(&core, now);
    ball_line_tick(&reader, now);

    core.output_mode = ppm_safety_ok() ? "PPM_YAW" : "NO_OUTPUT";

    while (Serial.available() > 0) {
        int value = Serial.read();
        now = millis();
        if (ball_line_feed(&reader, &core, value, now, reply, sizeof(reply))) {
            Serial.write(reply, strlen(reply));
        }
    }

    ppm_update(core.enabled, core.yaw);
}
